docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text: # Objective Source Assessed by 1 Learner can set up a new Bloom collection and navigate the Collection, Edit, and Publish tabs to locate a book's source files. Literacy Tools, 1.0 — Literacy Tools, Learner ("Demonstrates basic knowledge of literacy tools") Quiz Section 1 2 Learner can troubleshoot common Bloom problems (missing images, template mismatches, a collection that won't load) using Bloom's built-in diagnostic and reporting tools. Literacy Tools, 1.0 — Literacy Tools, Advanced Beginner ("Can use literacy tools and troubleshoot issues that arise") Quiz Section 1 3 Learner can create a simple picture book in Bloom from a template, adding illustrations and entering vernacular text. Literacy Tools, 2.0 — Creating Simple Books, Learner ("Learn to create and translate simple books with illustrations using recommended software") Scenario 1; Quiz Section 2 4 Learner can translate an existing simple book into another language using Bloom's multilingual/translation features. Literacy Tools, 2.0 — Creating Simple Books, Learner ("Learn to create and translate simple books with illustrations using recommended software") Scenario 1 5 Learner can apply advanced formatting and customization to a simple book (fonts, page layout, page size, styles). Literacy Tools, 2.0 — Creating Simple Books, Advanced Beginner ("Learn advanced formatting and customization of simple books with illustrations") Scenario 2; Quiz Section 2 6 Learner can select and configure the appropriate Bloom template (primer, decodable reader, or leveled reader) for a given literacy project. Literacy Tools, 3.0 — Creating primers, decodable or leveled readers, Learner ("Learn the tools used to create primers, decodable and leveled readers") Quiz Section 3 7 Learner can build a decodable reader in Bloom using the Decodable Reader Tool, configuring a letter/grapheme stage list. Literacy Tools, 3.0 — Creating primers, decodable or leveled readers, Advanced Beginner ("Learn to create primers, decodable readers, leveled readers, and comics using recommended software") Scenario 3; Quiz Section 3 8 Learner can build a leveled reader in Bloom, applying leveled-reader settings (word count and sentence-length limits) via the Leveled Reader Tool. Literacy Tools, 3.0 — Creating primers, decodable or leveled readers, Advanced Beginner ("Learn to create primers, decodable readers, leveled readers, and comics using recommended software") Scenario 3 9 Learner can set up Bloom's Talking Book tool to prepare a book for audio recording. Literacy Tools, 4.0 — Interactive Literacy Publications, Learner ("Learn available tools that make literacy interactive publication") Quiz Section 4 10 Learner can record and sync audio narration to text in Bloom to produce a talking/audio book with highlighted text. Literacy Tools, 4.0 — Interactive Literacy Publications, Advanced Beginner ("Create an audio book with highlighted text") Scenario 4; Quiz Section 4

docs.title: Assessment plan
docs.text: A 12-question quiz, grouped into four sections matching the lesson files (Bloom Basics & Troubleshooting; Simple Books & Translation; Primers, Decodable & Leveled Readers; Audio & Interactive Publications), with an 80% pass threshold (10/12), covers procedural recall and tool/template-selection judgment for objectives 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, and 10. The 4-scenario bank, sequenced foundational-to-complex (simple book creation/translation → formatting → decodable-to-leveled reader → talking book), is where hands-on software performance is actually verified and graded holistically against the mentor guide's rubric, covering objectives 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, and 10 — since a multiple-choice quiz can't confirm a learner actually operated the software, every "perform/configure" objective gets at least one scenario in addition to any quiz coverage. Objectives 4 and 8 (translation and leveled-reader configuration) are scenario-only, as they are best judged by inspecting the learner's output rather than by recall questions.

docs.title: SME knowledge notes
docs.text:
TODO (needs SME interview): No SME interview has been conducted yet for this module. Before content drafting begins, interview a Bloom-experienced SME and record here (verbatim where possible):

  • Real field cases (1–3 concrete stories): Actual language projects where Bloom was used to produce primers, simple books, decodable/leveled readers, or talking books — including any resource constraints (offline field locations, low-power devices, limited literacy of end users) or tool problems the SME personally encountered.
  • Common learner mistakes: What new Bloom users most often get wrong — e.g., template misuse, image/formatting pitfalls, mishandling multilingual book settings, decodable-reader grapheme-sequencing errors, or audio-sync problems.
  • What "good" looks like at 2 - With Assistance: What competent-with-support performance looks like in the field — e.g., what a consultant should be able to do for/with a literacy worker when creating a simple book, decodable reader, or talking book, and where a learner would still need guidance vs. work independently.
  • Tool-version specifics: Which Bloom version(s) and any relevant configuration/platform notes (Windows-only vs. other platforms, offline vs. online publishing, BloomPUB/BloomLibrary specifics) the SME flags as current gotchas.

Do not draft 01-*.md scenario content or lesson framing that depends on field specifics until this section is filled in from an actual SME interview.

docs.title: Handoff
docs.text:
• Learning objectives: 10, drawn directly from the Literacy Tools competency descriptor's Learner and Advanced Beginner activity-ladder rows across all four sub-components (1.0 Literacy Tools, 2.0 Creating Simple Books, 3.0 Creating primers/decodable/leveled readers, 4.0 Interactive Literacy Publications).
  • Modules: 3 numbered lesson files (45 + 35 + 25 = 105 minutes), each well under the 90-minute cap, plus a 30-minute scenario bank, a mentor guide, and a quiz (mentor guide and quiz excluded from seat time per convention).
  • Total learner seat time: 135 minutes (within the ≤270-minute ceiling and the smaller scope appropriate for a single stub-to-content conversion).

This document, once approved, is the contract for module-author and quiz-writer: they will draft only the modules, objectives, and assessments specified above — not freelance additional topics or competencies. The SME knowledge notes section must be completed before scenario-bank or lesson content that depends on field specifics is drafted.

This design is in Draft status and requires human approval before content drafting begins.

docs.title: How to review this
docs.text:
Read the whole package. Check facts, tool names, menu paths and versions against reality (stage 5), and the teaching, tone and ordering as if you were the learner (stage 6).

Leave feedback as a comment on the course's pull request (line by line on the Files changed tab) or on its tracker issue. You do not need to edit anything yourself.
